subject: physics

moments.title: Pauli's desperate proposal
moments.body: Beta decay seems to violate energy conservation. Pauli proposes a neutral, near-massless particle — the 'neutron' (he later calls it neutrino, 'little neutral one'). He famously writes: 'I have done a terrible thing, I have postulated a particle that cannot be detected.'
moments.takeaway: Pauli postulates a particle he believes nobody will ever see.

moments.title: Cowan and Reines detect neutrinos
moments.body: At the Savannah River nuclear reactor, Cowan and Reines detect the inverse beta decay of antineutrinos. They send Pauli a telegram. He responds: 'Thanks for message. Everything comes to him who knows how to wait.'
moments.takeaway: Pauli's 'undetectable' particle is detected 26 years later.

moments.title: Three neutrino flavours
moments.body: Brookhaven experiments show the muon has its own neutrino, different from the electron's. By 2000, the tau neutrino is also confirmed.
moments.takeaway: Three neutrino flavours match three lepton families.

moments.title: Neutrino oscillation
moments.body: Super-K shows atmospheric muon neutrinos transforming into tau neutrinos as they traverse Earth. SNO confirms solar electron neutrinos transform too. Neutrinos have mass — contradicting the original Standard Model.
moments.takeaway: Neutrinos oscillate. They have mass. The Standard Model is incomplete.

moments.title: Nobel for oscillation
moments.body: The 2015 Nobel goes to the Super-K and SNO leaders for proving neutrinos oscillate.
moments.takeaway: Neutrino mass is the first proven physics beyond the Standard Model.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Neutrino mass is < 0.8 eV (KATRIN, 2022). The mass hierarchy and CP violation in neutrinos are major experimental goals (DUNE, Hyper-K). About 100 trillion solar neutrinos pass through your body every second.
now.open_questions: Are neutrinos their own antiparticles (Majorana)? Why are their masses so small?

reflection: Pauli postulated an undetectable particle to save energy conservation. Was this sound science or special pleading?
